items.followUp: Compare a true solution and a colloid in four ways.

rubric.why: Particle size and visibility distinguish a suspension from a colloid.
rubric.description: Suspension particles are larger and visible to the naked eye, whereas colloidal particles are smaller and not visible to the naked eye.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the size comparison and 1 mark for the visibility comparison.

rubric.why: Settling and filtration show differences in the behaviour of the particles.
rubric.description: Suspension particles settle on standing and can be separated by ordinary filtration; colloidal particles remain dispersed and cannot be separated by ordinary filtration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the settling comparison and 1 mark for the filtration comparison.

rubric.why: Identifies the nature of both mixtures.
rubric.description: Both suspensions and colloids are heterogeneous mixtures, although a colloid may appear uniform.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both as heterogeneous mixtures.

modelAnswer: Suspension particles are larger than colloidal particles.
Suspension particles can be seen with the naked eye; colloidal particles cannot.
Suspension particles settle on standing; colloidal particles remain dispersed.
Suspension particles can be separated by ordinary filtration; colloidal particles cannot.
Both suspensions and colloids are heterogeneous mixtures, though a colloid may appear uniform.
